subject: Error in makegkParalleldcpp : negative length vectors are not allowed

messages.author: 6016d2d465399879
messages.subject: Error in makegkParalleldcpp : negative length vectors are not allowed
parts:
Hi everyone,

I hope someone can help me debug or at least explain an openCR error...

I am trying to fit a CJSsecr model to non-invasive genetic
sampling data covering a fairly large geographic area. I have been expressly asked to not share these data, so I have to
keep descriptions vague... The attached document contains *some*
summary information about the data which might be useful.

For the purpose of the analysis, I use a 20-km grid of "traps" over the whole
study area, and the following model fitting code :

    mod <- openCR.fit(
      dat,
      type = "CJSsecr",
      model = formX,
      mask = msk,
      detectfn = "HHR",
      movementmodel = "BVT",
      edgemethod = "truncate",
      details = list(
        CJSp1 = TRUE,
      )
    )

Models with a single built-in or user-provided covariate work fine, but as soon
as I include two covariates (for the same parameter, or 'across' parameters), I
get a segmentation fault (ie, R crashes), and / or the following error :

Error in makegkParalleldcpp(as.integer(data$detectfn), as.integer(.openCRstuff$sigmai[type]),  :
  negative length vectors are not allowed


For example, these formula / models work fine :

    form1 <- list(lambda0 ~ 1, sigma ~ 1, z ~ 1, phi ~ 1)
    form2 <- list(lambda0 ~ 1, sigma ~ Session, z ~ Session, phi ~ Session)

But these result in the error :

    form3 <- list(lambda0 ~ 1, sigma ~ 1, z ~ 1, phi ~ forest + Session)
    form4 <- list(lambda0 ~ 1, sigma ~ forest, z ~ 1, phi ~ Session)

The error message makes me think of some kind of too-big-an-object or out-of-memory
problem related to parallel computing, but it also happens if I force the use of
a single core...

If such an error is to be expected given the geographic range and fairly high
number of traps , and/or an inappropriate movement model for example, please let
me know...

I am a bit at a loss with respect to where to look / what to do next to debug or
explain the error... Any help or suggestion would be greatly appreciated!

Thank you in advance,

Olivier

messages.subject: Re: Error in makegkParalleldcpp : negative length vectors are not allowed
parts: OK, but you don't make it easy. I'm not clear whether we're dealing with one error or two. A trap covariate should not work in models for phi. You appear to have covariates with many levels - these can slow things down and demand extra space.  Size alone should not cause the errors, unless the product of the dimensions of an internal array gets ridiculous. Certainly openCR should not crash R - I can debug  given a minimal example that fails (my own example works). There's plenty you can do to make your own tests - drop HHR and BVT for a start. You have an extra comma in your code near the end.

messages.author: 118cea91a1619106
messages.subject: Re: Error in makegkParalleldcpp : negative length vectors are not allowed
parts:
Oliver

Thanks for sending example data that allowed me to find the source of the 'negative length vector' error. Turns out that the product of the dimensions of an internal array exceeded the allowed size of integer in R. I have added an explicit error message, now on GitHub. In your case it reads
Error: integer overflow in open.secr.loglifkn: 4667 parameter levels is too many given the numbers of detectors (1811) and mask cells (1949)
The code prepares a large array with size equal to the product of these dimensions, in your case 16472825213 (the largest integer allowed is about 2*10^9 - see ?as.integer). So you would need to reduce the number of parameter combinations by a factor of about 10 for it to work. I have yet to look into how you might do this.

The 'number of parameter levels' is the number of unique combinations of the levels of the different predictor variables. (Perhaps 'parameter' is misused here - may change that). I imagine the problem is the escalating number of unique combinations when predictors are combined, rather than the number of predictor variables per se.

Thinking aloud: Modelling spatial variation in phi is a hard problem because, conceptually, you would need to integrate over the possible unknown locations of animals between capture times and after last capture. Perhaps go down the Nimble path? Or partition your data according to first-capture location (I've just done this in another study)? (Most of your animals are in one clump, so chasing spatial effects may be unsatisfying). The CJSsecr model is messy because despite the name it's not a direct analogue of non-spatial CJS. I see why you would want to use it, but I don't think we (I) understand its limits.

I suggest using 'HEX' instead of 'HHR'. Failure with halfnormal (HHN) probably reflects the extreme improbability of distant detections under that model; HEX allows occasional long movements without requiring an extra parameter (HHR also leads to buffer-dependence, but that is probably not an issue for you).

Murray
